newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to resume talks on key pact with Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: Romania to resume talks on key pact with Ukraine.

text.p: Romania's Foreign Minister said on Saturday that Bucharest will offer "a compromise package" as part of resumed talks on a long-delayed treaty with neighbouring Ukraine.
"We have to show political determination to break the impasse in negotiations," Minister Adrian Severin told Reuters.

Kiev negotiators were expected here later on Saturday to relaunch talks on a post-communist pact, which bogged down last year over Romania's insistence that Ukraine denounce the 1939 Nazi-Soviet pact under which Bucharest lost territory.

"We did our best to resume the talks as soon as possible," said Severin, whose centrist coalition won last November's general and presidential elections, throwing leftists out of office for the first time in seven years.
Post-communist pacts resolving border and minority ethnic group issues between neighbours are a key condition for Romania and other east European countries bidding to join NATO as full members.
"We won't start the negotiations from the point where they were left by the previous government. That would mean getting back to the old stumbling points," Severin said.

"We will advance a compromise package in order to reach an acceptable solution for both sides," he said, declining to elaborate ahead of the talks -- led by the two countries' deputy foreign ministers -- which will officially resume on Monday.

Talks between the Black Sea neighbours broke up last year, when Kiev officials said Romania wanted references to lands lost to the Kremlin under the Nazi-Soviet pact which carved up large chunks of eastern Europe on the eve of World War Two.
Also in dispute is Serpent Island, a rocky outcrop off both countries' coast, handed to Moscow by Romania's Communist government in 1948.
Ukraine fears that any formal denunciation of the 1939 pact could prompt Romania to pursue its claims to lost territory.
Some 200,000 ethnic Romanians live in western districts in post-Soviet Ukraine, seized under that pact.
"We will have a flexible and pragmatic attitude...with the rights of ethnic Romanians in Ukraine and future cooperation prospects placed above historical issues," Severin said.
